To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the biaxially tensile strained Si nMOMS transistors down to 80nm gate length can be fabricated on relaxed SiGe substrated by in-situ doping.
biaxially stressed Si nMOS devices down to 80nm gate length were demonstrated and that the source to drain leakage was effectively reduced.

(i) the strain enhancement in Si MOSFETs is maintained down to 80nm gate length; (ii) in-situ dopes SiGe virtual substrats provide superior substrate junction leakage compared to conventional implantations; (iii) source to drain leakage is effectively reduced in 80 nm Si MOSFET devices by increment of channel dopings and rotation of channel direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of strained Si MOSFETs for the 45 nm technology node and beyond.
the investigation of biaxial strain in Si nMOS transistors on SiGe virtual substrata.
the development of high-performance SiGe virtual substrate based CMOS technology for future generations of microprocessors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biaxially stressed SiGe substrate technology is a very promising technology for future scaled MOSFET devices.
biaxially stressed Si nMOS with in-situ dopped virtual substrates is a very promising candidate for future technology nodes.
the leakage current in 80 nm strained devices can be reduced to levels that are comparable to the state-of-the-art 90 nm devices, and thus the strain-induced enhancement is preserved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the leakage currents in 80 nm Si nMOS devices on relaxed SiGe virtual substrats are comparable to conventional devices.
biaxially strain Si nMOS devices down to 80nm gate length are feasible.
biaxial stress is a viable option to enhance Si MOSFETs down into the 70 nm technology node and below.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leakage reduction is not a trivial task and requires careful design of device architecture.
biaxial stress engineering is an attractive approach to improve the performance of 80 nm Si nMOS devices.
80 nm bialxially strained nMOSFETS on relaxed SiGe virtual substrats are feasible with well controlled leakage current.
